Rewrite the five pages under agents/ — implementer.md, planner.md, researcher.md, reviewer.md, test-author.md — so each says everything it says now in fewer words: every requirement and prohibition survives, each rule stands once, sentences are short and imperative, and no reason runs past one sentence. Current word counts (wc -w, whole file): implementer 1095, planner 2203, researcher 1561, reviewer 2909, test-author 1134; each must end strictly below its number. The implementer edits ONLY the five pages. It never edits test-repo.sh: the five new word-cap cases there are the test-author's, and every existing case stays byte-identical because the plan keeps every phrase those cases grep for. Out of scope (later increments): rulebook.md, GEMINI.md, skills/**, .claude/rules/**, workflows/agile-loop.js, hooks/**.

METHOD. test-repo.sh holds dozens of cases that grep these pages for exact phrases, forbidden old wordings, per-line co-occurrences and paragraph structure. The design decision of this plan: keep every one of those keys verbatim and compress only the prose around them. Then no case is re-keyed, the re-key criterion holds vacuously, and the compression cannot silently unguard a rule. What is compressible: frontmatter descriptions (they count toward wc -w), connective and explanatory prose, and restatements a page makes twice. The keyed sentences are mostly the rules themselves in their measured winning form (prohibition + quoted excuse + one-sentence price, or a template) — .claude/rules/authoring.md is the form standard and loads when you open agents/* — so never rewrite a keyed rule out of that form. If a keyed sentence is the only thing left to shorten, leave it: a page a few words over its ideal still meets every criterion, and editing test-repo.sh is not yours. Work page by page; after each page run bash test-repo.sh (the inner loop this plan names — the judge stays bash test.sh) and repair any case you turned red before moving on. Before any edit, run the test-author's five word-cap cases and confirm each fails because its page still stands at its old count.

THE FIXED POINTS. Harvest the full literal key list from test-repo.sh before editing each page — every quoted grep pattern aimed at agents/*.md in these line ranges is a fixed point, and each case's comment names its Break: 185-191, 244-252, 327-350, 364-398, 449-470, 472-548, 550-584, 686-722, 724-764, 766-794, 2402-2427, 2429-2514, 2516-2602, 2604-2667, 2715-2781, 2783-2813, 3046-3067, 3252-3262, 3449-3676, 3678-4015. Presence patterns must survive character-for-character (many are matched against the page collapsed to one line with tr, so they may wrap across a line break but not change); absence patterns must never be reintroduced.

Page-wide word rules, all five pages: forbidden anywhere — 'rulebook'; 'handoff' in any spelling; 'argus', 'OTEL_', 'UROBOROS_OBS', 'collector'; 'probe' (reviewer.md alone owns it); 'chain depth' (planner.md alone); 'counts as tested' and 'dependency footprint' (the shared brief alone); 'exemption clause', 'rationalisation', 'occasion' (.claude/rules/authoring.md alone); the file names researcher.md, test-author.md, implementer.md, reviewer.md, planner.md, backlog.md except directly after a '/'. On implementer.md and test-author.md every physical line containing 'push' (any case, description included) must contain 'where its prompt asks for a push'. No sentence anywhere may describe deleting a branch from the remote.

Per-page constraints beyond the harvested greps. implementer.md: keep 'Never open `issue.md`' inside step 1 of '## How you work' — hooks/read-barrier.mjs cites it and test-repo.sh ~4010 pins the pairing; keep the collapsed-line phrases 'need a material decision' and 'leave a material decision open'; the already-red-failure rule is currently stated twice (end of step 4's aftermath paragraph and the `commands` bullet) — state it once, in the `commands` bullet. planner.md: keep the increment template block (it must still collapse to 'goal what it delivers', 'criteria its own acceptance criteria, one string each', 'depth its chain depth'), the three bold '**Where the review accepted it**'/'**Where the review did not accept it**'/'**Where the merge conflicts**' bullets, and the '<path> — <why the issue has to change it>' and '<criterion> → <increment id>' templates. researcher.md: keep the breaks/unbreakable templates, 'every criterion stands in exactly one of the two lists', 'a plan that needs no tests puts every criterion in unbreakable', the What and How case templates, 'at least one case', 'broken or removed', 'production change', 'mutation standard', 'suite doc', 'says so and why', and 'the implementer never sees it' on the testPlan bullet (read-barrier citation). test-author.md: keep 'CLAUDE.md', the cases-field template, 'take no other field of it' in step 1 (read-barrier citation), and one sentence saying why the frontmatter names a smaller model tier (.claude/rules/agents.md requires a page that names a tier to say why). reviewer.md — structure is load-bearing, not only wording: (1) keep the literal numbered lines '3. **The tests against the intent.**' and '4. **Beyond the criteria.**' — awk anchors — and check 3's own text must contain 'mutation standard' and 'no break'; (4) exactly one paragraph of the whole body may contain both 'pair of eyes' and 'break' — the opening paragraph, keep it so; (5) 'backlog.json' must share a physical line with 'never read'/'not read'/'without reading' (the heading '## You never read `backlog.json`' satisfies it — keep that heading, and keep 'the helper's reading subcommands are not yours' nearby, both cited by hooks/read-barrier.mjs) and 'backlog.json' must share a physical line with 'diff' (check 2's 'Where a changed file is `backlog.json`, it is not part of the diff you judge' — mind reflow); return.testPlan:
WHETHER. Tests, yes — but only five new cases. Every rule these pages carry is already pinned by existing test-repo.sh cases, the plan keeps their keys verbatim, and they go on guarding unchanged. The one criterion nothing yet guards is 'shorter than it was', and it gets one case per page.

WHAT — all five cases prove the criterion 'Each of agents/implementer.md, agents/planner.md, agents/researcher.md, agents/reviewer.md and agents/test-author.md is shorter than it was, measured in words':
1. agents/implementer.md — the file at HEAD → wc -w < agents/implementer.md prints a number strictly below 1095 → break: append the page's pre-compression body (git show <merge-base>:agents/implementer.md) below the current body so the count reaches 1095 again.
2. agents/planner.md — same shape → strictly below 2203 — break: same regrowth on planner.md.
3. agents/researcher.md — same shape → strictly below 1561 — break: same regrowth on researcher.md.
4. agents/reviewer.md — same shape → strictly below 2909 — break: same regrowth on reviewer.md.
5. agents/test-author.md — same shape → strictly below 1134 — break: same regrowth on test-author.md.
Edge: equality is failure — the pages stand at exactly these counts today, so assert -lt <old count>; that is also what makes each case red before the compression lands, which is the proof it works. Measure with wc -w < path (stdin form, so no filename lands in the output). Verify each number with that command before writing; where a measured count differs, the measured one wins — the criterion is 'shorter than it was'.

Criteria with no new case, and why — each omission is a decision:
- 'Everything the old text of these pages required is still required, and everything it forbade is still forbidden' — carried by the existing test-repo.sh cases, which turn red when a guarded rule is removed; the reviewer's named break for this criterion exercises one of them.
- 'Each page states each rule once, in short imperative sentences of common words; history, anecdotes and self-justification are gone, and no reason runs past one sentence' — deliberately untested: no computable predicate tells one rule worded twice from two rules, or a common word from a rare one; the reviewer reads each page against its merge-base text.
- 'Each page's role, audience, file location and English are unchanged' — the file-location half is carried by the existing plugin.json-agrees-with-agents/ case; role, audience and English are the reviewer's reading.
- 'Every test-repo.sh case keyed on wording these pages changed is re-keyed to the new wording and still turns red when its rule is removed; no case is deleted' — the plan changes no keyed wording, so no case is re-keyed and the existing cases' own Breaks still turn them red; whether a case was deleted is read off the test-repo.sh diff, which must hold nothing but the five added cases.
- 'bash test.sh exits 0' — the judging command itself; running it is the test.

HOW — every new case: integration (repository-fact check) — test-repo.sh at the repository root — plain bash, the file's own ok/no helpers — the command that runs just this file: bash test-repo.sh.
Suite conventions: test-repo.sh has no CLAUDE.md suite doc, deliberately — a CLAUDE.md beside it would sit at the repository root and load as project memory into every session and subagent, which this repository's architecture forbids (its rulebook reaches sessions through a hook for exactly that reason). Do NOT create one; this paragraph is the doc statement my page requires when the doc is missing. The file documents itself: a section opens with echo "=== <what the section pins>", each case is preceded by a comment naming the rule it pins and the Break that turns it red, and ok/no count passes and failures. Follow that style: append one new section at the end of the file — e.g. echo "=== the agent pages stay at their compressed size" — one comment plus if/ok/no block per page, the section comment citing docs/issues/2026-08-16-compress-the-rules and each case comment naming its Break (the regrowth above).
Prove the failures: run bash test-repo.sh once after writing. The five new cases must be the only new FAILs, each red because its page still stands at its old count — print the measured count in the no-message so the failure names itself. Quote the five FAIL lines in your return. Anything else red in the file goes in openQuestions and stays untouched.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE. Exactly one command, run from the repository root: bash test.sh. The list is closed.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED. This list is unrun — no decision in this plan turned on a fact only a run could settle, so the first runs are the test-author's failure proof and the implementer's inner loop. Expected shape once the tests land and before the compression: bash test-repo.sh red on exactly the five new cases.
breaks: Each of agents/implementer.md, agents/planner.md, agents/researcher.md, agents/reviewer.md and agents/test-author.md is shorter than it was, measured in words — append one page's pre-compression body (git show <merge-base>:agents/planner.md) below its current body so its wc -w count reaches its old count (2203 for planner.md) again; that page's word-cap case in test-repo.sh fails and bash test.sh exits 1.

Everything the old text of these pages required is still required, and everything it forbade is still forbidden — delete from agents/implementer.md the sentence beginning 'Never open `issue.md`' in step 1 of '## How you work'; test-repo.sh's case "the implementer's never-read-issue rule is a priced prohibition quoting its excuse" fails and bash test.sh exits 1.

Each page's role, audience, file location and English are unchanged — rename agents/reviewer.md to agents/review.md; test-repo.sh's case 'plugin.json declares every page in agents/ and nothing that is not there' fails and bash test.sh exits 1 (the role, audience and English halves are judged by reading, as the test plan says).

Every test-repo.sh case keyed on wording these pages changed is re-keyed to the new wording and still turns red when its rule is removed; no case is deleted — in test-repo.sh's agents/implementer.md codemap case (~line 466), change grep -qi 'codemap' to grep -qi 'codemapp', a key no page wording satisfies; that case fails and bash test.sh exits 1 (the no-case-deleted half is judged by reading the test-repo.sh diff, as the test plan says).

bash test.sh exits 0 — delete the breaks/unbreakable bullet from '## What you record' of agents/researcher.md; test-repo.sh's case 'agents/researcher.md gives both breaks and unbreakable their own template' fails and bash test.sh exits 1.
unbreakable: Each page states each rule once, in short imperative sentences of common words; history, anecdotes and self-justification are gone, and no reason runs past one sentence — no test can catch it: whether two differently worded sentences state one rule, whether a word is common, and whether a passage is self-justification are semantic judgements no grep, count or command computes; the reviewer judges it by reading each compressed page against its merge-base text.
rulings: Keep every grep key test-repo.sh already holds verbatim in the compressed pages, so no existing case is re-keyed and the re-key criterion holds vacuously, because re-keying dozens of literal keys multiplies suite-breakage risk for words the shorter-than-it-was criterion does not need; wrong costs a correction round re-keying the few cases a needed rewording touches.

Guard the shorter-in-words criterion with five new test-repo.sh cases capping each page strictly below its pre-compression wc -w count (1095, 2203, 1561, 2909, 1134), because that criterion needs a case that goes red when a page regrows and test-repo.sh owns repository facts; wrong costs deleting or re-capping five one-line cases.

Create no CLAUDE.md suite doc for test-repo.sh, because a repo-root CLAUDE.md loads as project memory into every session and subagent, which this repository's architecture forbids — the suite's conventions live in its own comments; wrong costs writing one doc later.

Frontmatter descriptions count toward the word measure and may be compressed under the same keyed constraints, because wc -w measures the file whole and the criteria address each page whole; wrong costs restoring a description sentence.
return.summary: Plan for compressing the five agent pages: keep every phrase test-repo.sh greps for verbatim and cut only the unkeyed prose, so no existing case needs re-keying; the test-author adds five word-cap cases (pages stand at 1095/2203/1561/2909/1134 words and must end strictly below), and bash test.sh alone judges the work.
